Mia Chen: Heads-up — ACME onboarding health check. Token burn spiked 2.5x in last 48h after they ramped embeddings. We need a quick preflight for the QBR deck and a short remediation plan if spend keeps running hot. cc @Raj for numbers
Raj Patel: Looking now. Current 48h burn = $12.8k, projected 30d at current rate = ~$192k. They have $50k credits left and retainer expires in 22 days. :eyes:
Samir Gupta: Do we have per-route breakdown? embeddings vs chat? That projection lumps everything. If embeddings are the driver we can suggest rerouting to smaller model or batching.
Raj Patel: Yep — embeddings = 68% of token cost. Chat = 22%, misc = 10%. Peak embeddings sequences are long (avg 1024 tokens).
Elena Torres: Customer feedback: they turned on near-real-time similarity search without batching because of latency concerns. They asked for enablement on cache + minibatch flows last week. We should include a short enablement offer in the QBR — 30m runbook + config changes.
Mia Chen: Good — two asks: (1) a short spend mitigation playbook to include in the QBR slide (safety-net thresholds, throttle recommendations, quick toggle steps) (2) an enablement offer to cut embeddings cost by target 40% w/o user-visible latency hit.
Samir Gupta: Draft mitigation snippet: ```json
{
  "policy": "safety-net",
  "thresholds": {
    "soft": 40000,
    "hard": 48000
  },
  "actions": {
    "soft": "email+notice-to-cs",
    "hard": "reduce-embeddings-rate-limit+fallback-to-quantized-model"
  }
}
```
Samir Gupta: Implementation note: we can wire the "reduce-embeddings-rate-limit" to a per-account routed policy that swaps to the q4-8bit variant and drops batch size from 256 -> 64. Should buy ~35-45% cost reduction.
Raj Patel: I'll run a quick forecast scenario with those knobs. If we apply quantized fallback + batch tuning their 30d projection drops from $192k -> $115k. Still need discussion on credits/retainer.
finance-bot: Account ACME789: current credits remaining = $50,000, monthly committed retainer = $12,000, expiration = 2026-04-13. Auto-renew flag = false.
billing-bot: ALERT: ACME789 spend rate crossed 70% of credits threshold at 1742109300. Notified account owner.
Elena Torres: For the QBR slide I'd like 3x things: 1) what happened (short bullets), 2) immediate mitigation we performed, 3) recommended next steps (enablement + updated commit ask). Also capture customer sentiment: they want predictable cost not surprise spikes.
Mia Chen: Action items: Raj — run the 3 scenario forecasts (status quo, quantized+batch, delay embeddings rollout) and paste numbers here by EOD. Samir — prepare the short policy snippet (json + two-line implementation steps) and add explicit rollback commands. Elena — draft the enablement 30m offer text and invite template for the customer. I'll own the QBR slide and negotiate renewal ask with AE.
Raj Patel: On it. Will post numbers in an attachment here (quick table).
Samir Gupta: Also adding quick rollback CLI for ops: ```bash
# swap model variant for embeddings
rwctl accounts set-model --account ACME789 --route embeddings --model "open-embed-q4-8bit" --batch-size 64
# revert
rwctl accounts set-model --account ACME789 --route embeddings --model "open-embed-fp16" --batch-size 256
```
Mia Chen: Perfect. If we can get the 40% cost delta in the deck we should be able to negotiate either a short retainer top-up or a staged commit. Please flag if the customer balks on commit.
Elena Torres: I'll draft an email that frames it as "predictability package" not a sell — includes the 30m enablement + one-time config tuning + 14-day monitoring window.
Raj Patel: Posted scenarios: status quo = $192k, quantized+batches = $115k, delay rollout (pause heavy indexing) = $84k. Notes: delay rollout hurts latency for some features.
Mia Chen: Thanks. Can we add one quick plot for the QBR showing projected runway under each scenario? Even a sparkline is fine.
Samir Gupta: I can generate a sparkline and upload. Also recommend we add an automated budget alert at 50% credits (soft) and 80% (hard) with automated throttle at hard.
Mia Chen: Agreed. Last thing — capture feedback loop: ask customer to share 3 sample workflows where they need low latency so we can tune batching safely. Elena please collect during enablement.
Elena Torres: Will collect and include in the QBR appendix. I'll ping the customer asap.
Mia Chen: Great — meeting at 4pm to finalize slides. :thumbsup:
Raj Patel: See you 4pm.
Samir Gupta: I'll bring the rollback runbook.
